Iran launched two waves of drone and ballistic missile attacks on Saturday night against four US bases in Bahrain, home to the US’ Fifth Fleet headquarters, the Iranian media reported, while Bahrain announced the attacks, warning the population to shelter.
Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency claimed that the Iranian military targeted four US bases in Bahrain, with two of the named as Sheikh Isa and Juffair, in what it called a response to continued US incursions in Iran’s airspace.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed that it struck 2 Patriot defence batteries and a radar system. Bahrain and the US military did not confirm the claims.
Bahrain said that its air defence intercepted several Iranian attacks, calling them a “heinous Iranian aggression”.
Local sources in Bahrain reported loud explosions and Bahrain’s Interior ministry announced that a fire broke out at a civilian industrial compound, with no injuries reported, while local videos showed smoke rising from a fire in an unidentified location.
Right after the attack on Bahrain, reports emerged from southern Iran of explosions in Sirik. The US military has retaliated regularly against Iranian military facilities in recent weeks.
Earlier on Saturday, US Central Command CENTCOM denied Iranian claims that a surface-to-air missile damaged a US F-16 fighter jet on Friday evening.
Meanwhile, at least three oil tankers were attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in what appeared to be the latest Iranian strikes on shipping through the strategic chokepoint.
In a sharp increase of incidents in the Strait of Hormuz over the last week, the UK military’s maritime security center (UKMTO) said two tankers were struck separately by projectiles early Saturday while exiting the Persian Gulf through the strait. There were no reports of casualties.
The Iranian navy said in a statement carried on state media that a tanker hit a naval mine east of the strait and caught fire. State media also said that the military carried out its most “intense and varied” operations yet in the strait overnight to stop vessels.
Iran’s army spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia warned the US again on Saturday that any attack on Iran will be met with “a decisive and immediate response” as “we are much stronger than in the past,” Iranian TV IRIB report.
“Any new aggression will be met with a decisive, immediate and effective response from the armed forces, and the defence of the country will not be limited to a specific geographical area,” Akraminia said during a visit to Iranian troops in the south of the country.
The Iranian TV showed for the first time the ground troops deployed into defensive positions in the coastal areas of southern Iran on Saturday.
Meanwhile on Saturday, as more than 14 Iranian tankers are reported to be prepared off Kharg Island to break out of the US military blockade in the coming days, Iran’s deputy minister of foreign affairs Kazem Gharibabadi told Iranian media that the US blockade of Iranian ports “is an act of war and we will take any necessary measures to break this economic siege.”
Iran warned of a “fierce military response” if the convoy was engaged by the US military, threatening with widespread attacks on energy infrastructures across the Gulf region.
Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian also said that Iran is subject to a “silent economic war” which is “tougher than a war with missiles,” adding that Iran has the capability to withstand it.
As Gharibabadi announced that Tehran has warned the United States that the Iranian convoy will sail soon to China, the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War said that “Iranian attempts to run the blockade impose a series of dilemmas on the United States by either collapsing the blockade or returning to a war that imposes unideal political costs on the United States by straining its relationships with Gulf allies.”
Against the backdrop of the intensifying crisis, the diplomatic negotiations between the US and Iran spearheaded by Qatar continue.
Iran’s deputy foreign minister Gharibabadi announced on Saturday that a Qatari delegation held talks with Iranian officials on Friday evening for some two hours, before returning to Doha.
Iranian Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi suggested that a deal is possible when he declared that reopening the Strait of Hormuz would be “not difficult” if the US accepted Iran’s “reasonable conditions,” especially by ending the blockade which he called “completely illegal,” lifting sanctions and Washington acknowledging “past mistakes.”
In parallel, US president Donald Trump told US network Fox News on Saturday that he planned to make a “permanent” deal with Iran to prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon and that he was never interested in a regime change in Iran.
“I intend to reach a permanent deal with Iran that prevents them from obtaining nuclear weapons, even if another president takes my place in the future and is unfit for the office,” Trump said.

GUASAVE, Mexico (AP) — Heavy gunfire, helicopters and burning trucks marked Mexico's Sinaloa state Saturday after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," in an operation that left at least 11 people dead.
Meza Flores, one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured and flown to Mexico City on Saturday after the firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen overnight left residents of the city of Guasave terrorized.
This undated image released by the U.S. Department of State shows Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores. U.S. Department of State via AP hide caption
Mexico's Defense Ministry on Saturday afternoon said that seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed.
The capo climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization. The United States had a $5 million reward offer for information leading to his arrest, and he was wanted for trafficking drugs to the U.S. and illegally carrying firearms.
Mexico's government said in a report early Saturday that intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture him, but provided few details about how authorities in Mexico and the United States coordinated to detain Meza Flores.
He was also a key ally to "Los Mayos," a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which was designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the Trump administration last year. His capture represents a blow to the cartel as it fights with another faction for control of the northern Mexican state.
Authorities in the United States and Mexico celebrated the arrest as a security win. U.S. President Donald Trump has pressured Mexico's government to go after criminal groups.
As a fierce firefight settled into a tense calm Saturday, experts warned that picking off capos could set off another wave of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring cartel factions.
Mexican forces' move against cartel fuels violence The capture of Meza Flores and his No. 2 in the city of Guasave, Sinaloa, set off a wave of violence when a firefight broke out around 7 p.m. on Friday, according to residents of the 290,000-person municipality. Soon, military helicopters and drones were flying overhead, and helicopters opened fire on key locations across the city.
Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below. Such shows of force by cartels are common following the capture or killing of leaders.
"The fighting was happening all over Guasave," said Alma Camacho, a Guasave resident and local journalist. "It spread throughout the city."
Mexican authorities said that they used "stealth and surprise" to arrest Meza Flores, establishing a security perimeter around the building where he was located. After coming under attack with guns and explosives from suspected cartel operatives, armed forces personnel entered a home and detained him.
Video shared by Mexico's Defense Ministry shows Meza Flores and two others being marched by heavily armed soldiers onto a military aircraft to appear before prosecutors in Mexico City. A total of eight people were detained, according to authorities.
Because of the violence, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4 a.m. on Saturday, said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorized to discuss the case.
"Getting him (Meza Flores) out was extraordinary," the official said, describing an intense response by members of the criminal group who maintained at least "10 roadblocks" with burning vehicles on Guasave's streets.
Terror in Sinaloa Guasave resident and firefighter Paola Sánchez said that thousands of people were terrorized late Friday as they took shelter from intense gunfire in grocery stores and other locations.
"Last night, many businesses were burned ... along with cars and trucks," Sánchez told The Associated Press.
She said that the city's firefighters had to take shelter at their station and wait until Saturday morning for orders from their superiors to dispatch the first crews to check whether any businesses or vehicles were still burning.
An uneasy calm seemed to settle over the city Saturday. Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch wrote on X on Saturday morning that armed forces would remain deployed in Sinaloa state to protect civilians. He lamented the deaths of the four soldiers killed in the operation.
Burned-out trucks continued to line the freeway leading into the town, blocking roadways on Saturday.
"The aftermath of last night's war still lingers. Burned cars in the streets, several Oxxo stores completely burned down," Camacho said, referring to a chain of convenience stores in Mexico.
Guasave residents remained "very afraid" because security forces were absent from the streets, Camacho said.
Capture prompts celebration and warnings Meza Flores' detention marks another high-profile capture of a cartel leader as Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum faces pressure from Trump to crack down on cartels. Sheinbaum has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors, and homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.
The U.S. and Mexican governments celebrated the capture on Saturday, with the DEA commending Mexican authorities.
"Results like these don't happen overnight. They are built on sustained cooperation and trust. This is what partners can accomplish together," U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said in an X post. "We will continue the hunt."
Mexican Security Secretary García Harfuch called the detention "an important step in pacifying Sinaloa."
Sheinbaum's government has targeted a number of cartel kingpins , including Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes , known as " El Mencho ," who was killed by the military in February.
Mexican security analyst David Saucedo said that the capture of Meza Flores marked another case of the governments of Mexico and the U.S. increasingly falling back on a longstanding security strategy that critics warn could fuel more violence in the long run.
The so-called kingpin strategy relies on zeroing in on capos like Meza Flores as a way to combat cartels. But experts say that it often triggers violent power disputes among groups, like the one underway in Sinaloa.
"What is evident is this is a product of pressure from the United States," Saucedo said. "What they do is capture high-profile kingpins — the leaders — but they don't dismantle the entire organization. They arrested the No. 1 and No. 2, but the entire network of hit men, street-level drug dealers, businesses and political and police connections remains intact."

Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
A second sticking point involves a push from the Africa Group to get commitments on more money for adaptation - but the EU has previously said it would not support this.
Negotiating teams due to fly out on Sunday morning are now moving their flights to Monday in a sign that a deal is not yet in sight.
If countries cannot reach consensus - which is required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended.
In that case the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year. This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995.
Panama's Environment Minister is pushing for language on fossil fuels to be in the final agreement
On Saturday, EU Commissioner for Climate Wopke Hoekstra said if the bloc could not get "what is needed in terms of climate action... then there's no deal."
The UK's chief negotiator, Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, remained more hopeful and said her team was still working to get an agreement.
"These are difficult negotiations, but discussions remain productive and there is a deal to be done. The UK is pushing hard for an outcome and we will keep working in the coming hours to bring countries together."
Another risk is that negotiating teams have to start journeys home, and the meeting could lose the critical number of nations needed to pass any global agreement.
More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
Ministers from Panama, Solomon Islands, Cote d'Ivoire and the EU are fighting to get a commitment to move away from oil, gas and coal back into the final agreement after fossil fuel producers led by Saudi Arabia pushed for its removal.
"It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels and we simply will not put up with it," said Juan Carlos Navarro, Panama's minister for the environment.
His words were echoed by France's Minister of Ecological Transition, Monique Barbut.
She took aim at several references in the text to carbon capture, use and storage - the technology that takes emissions when they are released and stores them underground - as a licence for other countries to keep burning oil and gas.
"We cannot be announcing to the world that we are now getting to 1.5 increase in the temperature and do business like nothing was happening," Barbut said.
For the first time at a COP the agreement - known officially as the Antalya Accords - could acknowledge that the goal of keeping global temperature rise below 1.5C has been missed.
Beyond this point scientists warn , external that millions more people will be exposed to sea level rise and extreme heat.
But Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister who is leading negotiations, pushed back on the need to include language on fossil fuels.
He argued that this summit was about implementation, and should focus on the move towards clean energy sources.
Away from COP, renewable energy is growing at unprecedented rates. For the first time this year a modern renewable source - solar panels - was the biggest contributor to meeting new global energy demand , outstripping oil and gas , external .
The International Energy Agency also warned this week that the longer disruption to fuel supplies through the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran War continues, the stronger the incentive to switch to electricity powered by renewables.
Although, this week US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed at a meeting in Shenzhen to increase oil production in the face of fuel supply disruption.
It is understood that one proposal is to keep fossil fuels off the table in exchange for Saudi Arabia and other petro-states signing up to a pledge for 35% of their energy consumption to come from electricity by 2035.
This does not solve one of the other key issues raised by developing nations - the lack of money.
Earlier versions of the text included an agreement to ramp up money for adaptation to $120bn (£91bn) by 2035 - that figure has now been removed.
"We did not come here to beg, we came here to claim what is rightfully ours for our people who are suffering the brunt of anthropogenic activities of developed countries," said Zanetor Agyeman Rawlings, Ghana's Environment Minister and chair of the African Group of negotiators.
Climate activists and environmental groups, who are observers to these talks, have slammed negotiations.
"I can tell you without any doubt that this has been the worst COP ever," said Mohamed Adow of Powershift Africa.
These groups are normally highly critical of the process for not moving fast enough. But it seems that Turkey have been particularly unpopular as co-hosts after their lead negotiator walked out of some crucial negotiations leaving many countries feeling "disrespected", said one observer.

Brazil’s former President Jair Bolsonaro is in intensive care after being diagnosed with an acute bowel obstruction, according to the DF Star hospital where he is being treated.

Tens of thousands of people marched in cities in France on Saturday, on the sixth weekend in a row of protests to demand better public services and express anger over the rising cost of living and inequality.
The protest movement, sparked in mid-September by high school students demanding better learning conditions, fuelled a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality that spread across Europe, even as turnout in France has dwindled.
Across the country, organisers reported 150,000 protesters, compared to 200,000 last week and 800,000 on the first one held October 17.
The interior ministry said numbers had "significantly declined", counting 82,500 people, compared to 106,000 last Saturday.
Read more Interior ministry says 82,500 people protest across France, unions claim 150,000
Thousands of people gathered in central Paris's Place de la République square in a festive atmosphere, with musicians playing, food trucks, costumes and homemade signs, before marching east through the city.
Flags and vests of trade unions and left-wing parties mingled with those of student organisations and the Yellow Vest movement, which is marking its anniversary eight years after it rattled President Emmanuel Macron 's government.
One group had set up mock headstones proclaiming the death of France's public services, including social security and education.
"In a number of countries, young people are going through the same thing, namely precarity. You have to choose between having a roof over your head, getting medical care, and being able to eat your fill," said Manon Moret, general secretary of the students' union Unef.
On Friday crowds rallied across multiple countries to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.
"I want to live, not survive," read one placard held by a protester in Paris.
Another read: "No to the licence to kill", in reference to a law adopted by France's parliament on Friday increasing protection for law enforcement officers using their weapons, heavily criticised by the left.
The protests have been largely peaceful but have seen fringe violence and accusations of police brutality.
At least 31 people have been seriously injured by security forces since the protests began, according to a count by AFP based on direct testimonies, victims' lawyers and NGO records. Authorities have not provided an official toll.
Last month, some rallies across France degenerated into clashes between riot police and demonstrators, with shops looted and buildings attacked and torched.
Read more Latest cost-of-living protests bring more than 140,000 onto the streets across France
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had warned regional authorities to be "particularly vigilant regarding the groups most hostile to law enforcement" after the police law was adopted.
Protesters marched on Saturday in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast.
Clashes broke out on the sidelines of some protests as people tried to rally in banned areas, set fire to vehicles and bins, with police firing tear gas.
Unions and activists have called for more protests in the coming weeks.
Avril Bas, who attended the Paris protest with her knitting group to support high school students' demands for better learning conditions, was not discouraged by the lower turnout on Saturday.
"If we take care of our young people, our students, we'll have a wonderful tomorrow and that's why I'm here," the 27-year-old told AFP.
"We'll be there next week and the next week and as long as we're needed," she said.

US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim
At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic.
In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.
“I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said. “I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing, that if it were asked, I would have said that: ‘Would you do it again?’ And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.”
However, Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to developing a nuclear weapon this year that it was necessary to go to war, which he has made dozens of times in the past nine months, is undermined by public evidence and contradicts his own previous statements on US strikes against Iranian facilities in 2025.
At a campaign rally in Alaska last month, Trump insisted that he had to join Israel in attacking Iran in February because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”.
That claim appears at odds with what his then director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, testified to Congress on 25 March 2025, two months into Trump’s second term: that US intelligence agencies reported that Iran had not tried to make a nuclear weapon for more than two decades. The US intelligence community, Gabbard said, “continues to assess Iran is not building a nuclear weapon and supreme leader Khamenei has not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003”.
Despite that assessment, three months later, on 21 June 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities. The strikes, Trump told the public that night , “were a spectacular military success. Iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated.”
Eight months after that, however, when Trump announced the start of a full-scale war on Iran early on 28 February 2026, he said in a video statement from Mar-a-Lago the war was necessary to “ensure that Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon”.
The morning after this month’s midterm elections, Vance said in a statement posted on social media: “The reason we lost is the war.”
“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so,” he added. “Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost.”
In the White House briefing room on Friday, after Trump said that Vance should have said the war was necessary, a reporter asked the vice-president whether he would argue that the war in Iran was worth it.
In his response, Vance said it was not his place to second-guess the president, but refrained from actually endorsing Trump’s claim that the war was essential to stop Iran from creating a nuclear weapon.
“Look, what I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing. It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, of innocent people,” Vance said. “I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again.”
“My view is that my goal is, and my job is, to support the president of the United States,” the vice-president said.
The vice president’s office did not respond to a request to comment.

Police say the boat driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.
A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of attendees to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people, according to authorities.
The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, according to police.
“So far, 24 bodies have been recovered from the scene of the incident, while search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for the National Emergency Management Agency, said on Saturday.
Two children were among the four bodies initially recovered from the water on Friday, police said at the time, adding that 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic and five taken to hospital in the state capital.
Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told the Reuters news agency there were at least 300.
Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.
According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district.
The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”.
Such boat accidents are common on Nigeria’s busy rivers and waterways, often caused by overloaded vessels, poor maintenance, or failure to comply with safety regulations.
A similar incident occurred in August, when at least 51 people died after a boat sank in northwest Nigeria’s Sokoto State . In another incident, in January, at least 26 people drowned after a boat ferrying people from Jigawa to Yobe State capsized.

The sergeant, who was shot, fired his weapon a number of times after alleged ‘targeted’ attack outside island’s police station
Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast
A police officer who was shot outside a remote Tasmanian police station is alleged to have shot and killed his attacker in response to what authorities believe was a “targeted” incident.
Tasmania police deputy commissioner, Jonathan Higgins, said the sergeant had just come off shift at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, which is north-east of the Tasmanian mainland. He had parked and gotten out of his police vehicle when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday, Higgins told reporters on Sunday.
Investigators sent to investigate the shooting of the sergeant discovered the body of a man, aged in his mid-20s, on Walker Street a few hundred metres from the police station.
Police believe he was shot by the sergeant, who fired his weapon a number of times.
“At this early stage in the investigation, police believe this was a targeted incident,’” Higgins said.
On Sunday afternoon the sergeant was in the operating theatre undergoing surgery at the Royal Hobart hospital and remained in a serious but stable condition.
He is one of three officers stationed on Flinders Island and has worked there for a number of years.
Whitemark has a population of about 300 according to the 2021 census, and the entire population of Flinders Island is fewer than 1,000 people.
Extra police resources, including forensic and uniformed officers, have been deployed to the island. Those with information about these incidents, including CCTV or dashcam footage of Walker Street, have been urged to contact police.
Police are hoping to speak to the family of the deceased man.
Higgins said it was “the nature of our work” for police to receive threats from the public.
The Tasmanian premier, Jeremy Rockliff, has been in contact with the state’s police commissioner, Donna Adams, who attended the Hobart hospital as the shot sergeant undergoes treatment.
“My thoughts are with everyone affected by this horrific incident, including the police officer, their family and colleagues,” Rockliff said.
“Our police officers work every single day to keep Tasmanians safe, and incidents like this are a stark reminder of the risks they face in the line of duty.”
It is the second shooting of an on-duty police officer in Tasmania in 18 months. A Tasmanian officer was killed in the state’s north-west in June 2025 while executing a court-issued warrant to repossess a residence. The occupant of the home pleaded guilty to murder.

A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.
The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a new chapter in economic relations between the two sides.
"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen , president of the European Commission, said at the signing ceremony on Saturday.
"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.
The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) are designed to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.
The agreement comes after almost 10 years of negotiations and is part of a wider series of trade deals by the EU .
The bloc hopes to reduce its reliance on individual economic partners as trade with both China and the US has become more difficult in recent years.
Von der Leyen also stressed the importance of international cooperation, saying that "in a time when others are closing their doors, we keep ours open."
The deal sees tariffs on about 98% of EU exports to Indonesia to be done away with. The EU estimates that European companies could save more than €600 million (around $658 million) per year.
"The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto said, hailing a "new chapter" in economic relations with the EU. He said the deal would benefit his country’s main exports to Europe, including palm oil, footwear and textiles.
Palm oil and deforestation had been major stumbling blocks during the negotiations, and the agreement includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address environmental concerns.
The EU parliament is now expected to greenlight the deal while Indonesian authorities will also complete the ratification process so it can enter into force in 2027.

Maçın sonunda Okan Buruk, 4. hakem Fatih Tokail'le konuşmasının ardından önce sarı, ardından kırmızı kart gördü. Buruk kurallar gereği konuşamadığı için basın toplantısına yardımcı antrenör İrfan Saraloğlu geldi. Galatasaray , Samsunspor karşılaşmasını RAMS Park yerine Başakşehir Fatih Terim Stadyumu'nda oynadı.
Saraloğlu, kartların maçın hemen ardından yaşanan bir tokalaşma anında gösterildiğini söyleyerek tepkisini dile getirdi. Teknik direktörün sahaya girişini ve hakemle yaşanan anı şu sözlerle anlattı:
“Maçla ilgili gözlemlerimizi bir kenara atmakta yarar var. Maçın yorumunu yapacak kişinin buradan uzaklaştırılmasına anlam veremiyorum. Hocamız oyuncularını tebrik etmek için sahaya yöneldi ve yakındaki hakemin elini sıktı. Sonra da sahaya yöneldi ama hakem benim elimi sıkmadı diye arka arkaya kartlar gösterdi. Bu da bizi düşündürdü.”
Saraloğlu konuşmasının devamında maç sonu yaşananların takımın odağını bozmayacağını vurguladı ve gözünü Şampiyonlar Ligi 'ndeki bir sonraki maça çevirdi. Basın toplantısında mikrofonda olmaktan memnun olmadığını da belirten Saraloğlu, kırmızı kartın Galatasaray cephesinde üzüntü yarattığını kabul etti. Sözlerinin devamı şöyle:
“Burada olmak benim için keyifli değil. Önümüzde Şampiyonlar Ligi maçı var. Tüm konsantrasyonumuzu bu maça verdik. Kırmızı kart bizi üzdü ama yolumuzdan dönmeyeceğiz ve şampiyon olacağız. Şampiyonlar Ligi'nde de Türkiye'yi başarıyla temsil edeceğiz.”

A Russian strike on the center of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky ’s hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.
Meanwhile, a Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad caught fire in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday after it was hit by drones , Finnish and Russian officials said. It was not clear who struck the ship not far from the Russian border. The Finnish prime minister warned that the war was spilling into the region.
Read more Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday night on Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine , Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram. Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said 60 people were wounded, including six children.
The strike caused four fires and damaged about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, as well as businesses and vehicles, Vilkul said.
Video footage published by the regional branch of the Ukrainian State Emergency Service appeared to show further strikes while ambulance and firefighting crews were responding at the scene, as fires burned around them.
“First, two ballistic missiles. And then, when the emergency and rescue operation began, three more rockets hit doctors, rescuers and utility workers,” Vilkul wrote on Telegram.
The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington. It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland , in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country.
In the unprecedented two-week military exercise that began November 9 in southeastern Poland, forces are preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military. European countries previously have expressed alarm at what they deem to be Russia’s attempts to destabilize the continent.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte , speaking to reporters in Warsaw on Saturday, called the airspace violation “dangerous” and said all allies stood “in full solidarity with Poland.”
“NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory,” Rutte said. He said the alliance functioned “as it should” on Friday morning, when NATO jets supported Polish F-16s scrambled as Russian objects approached Polish airspace. NATO’s top military commander was assessing the alliance’s defenses and would make adjustments if needed, Rutte said.
The head of NATO forces ⁠in Europe, General Alexus Grynkewich, would do everything necessary to identify any threats to defense and deterrence capabilities ​and would implement appropriate adjustments if needed, Rutte ‌said.
On Monday, a meeting of ​NATO's North Atlantic Council will be held ​in Brussels to discuss the violation of Polish airspace by Russian missiles, PAP also ​reported on Saturday.
"In the near future, we will receive strong support from our NATO allies to bolster the protection of our eastern border," Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz wrote on X ⁠on Saturday, commenting on the meeting of the NATO body.
"I've been in ⁠contact today ​with general Grynkewich, to coordinate the details of these measures."
Zelensky on Saturday reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.
"Of course Ukraine very much wants to be in NATO," Zelensky told reporters, judging that membership of the alliance was one of the "most obvious security guarantees" for his country.
The issue of Ukraine joining NATO, ruled out by Washington since 2025, resurfaced in recent days during fresh talks to end the war nearly five years after Russia's invasion.
At a meeting with Kyiv's allies in Berlin on Thursday, US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington could be ready to grant Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty.
That clause -- the cornerstone of NATO -- states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all allies.
At a meeting with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv, Zelensky said Saturday that Ukraine’s repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland were a “fair response” to scores of Russian attacks on Ukrainian bridges. He said that Russia President Vladimir Putin had "attacked Ukrainian bridges 109 times.”
“Not the number of missiles — the number of attacks,” he said. “This is important, that’s why it’s our absolutely fair response.”
The Ukrainian leader said Putin “doesn’t want to stop the war” and is looking to escalate. He also rejected Putin’s claim that the Kerch bridge is used exclusively by civilian traffic.
“If he can use internet, he can use it and see tanks, armored vehicles, artillery,” the Ukrainian leader said.
Read more Ukraine critically damages bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia
Streeting called the airspace violations in Poland “an outrageous provocation” and urged allies to respond by stepping up support for Ukraine. “The more they try and deter Europe from supporting Ukraine, the more we will step up,” he said.
The drone incursion in Poland stoked tensions between Europe and Moscow just as the U.S. tries to add momentum to talks it is mediating on ending the war that began with Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.
US President Donald Trump discussed the war with Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a summit in China on Thursday, according to his envoy Steve Witkoff . Trump called Putin his “friend” during the meeting and continued to tout their relationship at a White House news conference Friday.
Asked about Trump’s remarks in an interview with CNN, Zelensky called Putin “a killer.”
“For us, he is an enemy. And of course, for us, he is a killer,” Zelensky said Friday. He warned that describing the Russian leader in friendly terms could mean “he doesn’t feel enough pressure.”
Elsewhere in Ukraine, 11 people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday. One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.
In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Başta 2020 yılında İngiliz kraliyet ailesindeki görevlerini bırakıp ABD'ye taşınmaları kelimenin tam anlamıyla bir bomba etkisi yarattı.
Sonra yaptıkları açıklamalar, Harry'nin ailesine yönelttikleri suçlamalar derken dikkat çektikçe çekti Sussex çifti. NEDEN APAR TOPAR DÖNDÜKLERİ MERAK KONUSUYDU Ama sonra bu yılın ağustos ayında hiç kimsenin beklemediği bir gelişme yaşandı. Harry ve Meghan, çocukları Archie ile Lilibet'i de alıp İngiltere'ye döndüler.
Tabii ki bu ani dönüş merak uyandırdı. Nedenleriyle ilgili bir sürü söylenti ortalarda dolaşıyor hala.
Bazıları Harry'nin memleketini özlediğini ileri sürdü. Bazıları da kanser olan babası Kral Charles'a yakın olmak istediğini öne sürdü.
Bütün bunlar olabilir elbette. Ama son dönemde bir iddia var ki kesinlikle Sussex çiftinin apar topar, kaçarcasına İngiltere'ye dönmelerine mantıklı bir açıklama olabilir.
'VİZE BİTTİ, DÖNDÜLER' İDDİASI Buna göre Harry'nin ABD vizesi bittiği ve hemen yenilenmediği için çift İngiltere'ye gitme kararı aldı.
Bazı kaynaklar Harry'nin bu vize durumunun, ani bir şekilde İngiltere'ye dönüşte büyük etkisi olduğunu söylüyor.
Page Six'in haberine göre ABD hükümetinden bir kaynak "Harry'nin vizesinin süresi doldu ve hemen yenilenmedi" dedi.
Eski bir ABD Dışişleri Bakanlığı yetkilisi de "Tüm vizelerin bir son kullanma tarihi olur. Bunların düzenli olarak yenilenmesi gerekir" diye bu görüşü destekledi.
SORUN ÇÖZÜLDÜ, NOEL'DE ABD'YE GİDİYORLAR Bu arada yine Page Six'in haberine göre Harry, göçmen vizesi yenilenmediği için ailesini alıp ağustos ayında apar topar İngiltere'ye dönse de sonradan bu sorun çözüldü.
Çünkü son dönemde konuşulanlara göre Sussex çifti, Noel tatilini Meghan Markle 'ın ailesiyle birlikte California'daki malikanelerinde geçirmeyi planlıyor.
Bu arada yeri gelmişken her ne kadar çocukları Archie ve Lilibet, İngiltere'de okula başlasa da Meghan ve Harry, ABD'deki malikanelerini de kapatmadı.

Telefon ekranını uzaklaştırmak, markette ürün etiketini ışığa tutmak veya bilgisayarda çalışırken gözlük değiştirmek zamanla alışkanlığa dönüşür. Özellikle 40’lı yaşlardan sonra gözün doğal lensinin esnekliğini kaybetmesi, yakına odaklanmayı güçleştirir. Bu değişim, yaşa bağlı yakın görme sorunu yani presbiyopi olarak bilinir.
Yakın gözlüğü bu ihtiyacı karşılayabilir. Ancak günlük yaşamını gözlüğe daha az bağımlı sürdürmek isteyen kişiler için farklı seçenekler de bulunuyor. Günümüzde göz içi lens teknolojileri, uygun hastalarda gözlüğe duyulan ihtiyacı azaltmaya yönelik olanaklar sunuyor.
‘Ömürlük lens’, doğal lensin yerine cerrahi olarak yerleştirilen ve uzun süre göz içerisinde kalmak üzere tasarlanan bir göz içi lens ürünüdür. Dikkat çeken özelliklerinden biri, kişinin farklı mesafelerdeki görme ihtiyaçlarının ameliyat öncesinde planlanabilmesidir.
GÜNLÜK HAYATTA FARKLI MESAFELERDE GÖRME Bir kitap sayfasındaki satırlarla bilgisayar ekranı veya karşı kaldırımdaki tabela aynı uzaklıkta değildir. Gün içerisinde gözlerimiz sürekli farklı mesafelere odaklanır.
Tek odaklı göz içi lensler belirli bir mesafede görmeyi hedeflerken, çok odaklı ve trifokal lens seçenekleri uygun hastalarda yakın, orta ve uzak mesafelerde gözlük ihtiyacını azaltmak amacıyla değerlendirilebilir.
Ömürlük lens, kontakt lens gibi sabah takılıp akşam çıkarılmaz. Günlük temizleme, solüsyon kullanma veya belirli aralıklarla rutin yenileme gerektirmez. Bu özellik, günlük yaşamda kullanım kolaylığı sağlayabilir.
Özellikle telefon kullanmak, kitap okumak, bilgisayarda çalışmak ve uzak mesafedeki nesneleri görmek gibi aktivitelerde gözlüğe daha az ihtiyaç duyulması, kişinin yaşam konforuna katkıda bulunabilir.
UZUN SÜRELİ KULLANIMIN EKONOMİK AVANTAJI Gözlük numarası değiştiğinde camların yenilenmesi, yeni çerçeve alınması veya yakın ve uzak için ayrı gözlük kullanılması gerekebilir. Kontakt lens kullananlarda ise düzenli ürün ve bakım ihtiyaçları bulunur. Yıllar içerisinde tekrarlanan bu harcamalar, gözlük kullanımının ekonomik boyutunu oluşturur. Ömürlük lensin göz içerisinde uzun süre kalması ve rutin olarak değiştirilmemesi, uzun vadeli kullanım açısından önemli bir avantajdır.
Uygun hastalarda gözlüğe duyulan ihtiyacın azalması, yeni gözlük camları ve çerçeveler için yapılan harcamaların da azalmasına katkıda bulunabilir. Böylece ömürlük lens, günlük yaşam konforunun yanında uzun vadede ekonomik fayda sağlayabilecek bir seçenek olarak öne çıkar. Bu değerlendirmede cerrahi işlem ve takip ihtiyaçlarının da dikkate alınması önemlidir.
KATARAKT VE GÖZ İÇİ LENS UYGULAMALARI Katarakt, gözün doğal lensinin saydamlığını kaybetmesiyle ortaya çıkar. Görme bulanıklaştığında yalnızca gözlük numarasını değiştirmek yeterli olmayabilir. Katarakt ameliyatında bulanıklaşan doğal lens çıkarılır ve yerine yapay göz içi lens yerleştirilir. Bu aşamada kişinin ameliyat sonrasında hangi mesafelerde görmeye öncelik verdiği de değerlendirilir.
Kataraktı olmayan ancak yaşa bağlı yakın görme güçlüğü yaşayan bazı kişilerde de doğal lens değişimi gündeme gelebilir. Bu nedenle ömürlük lens, yalnızca katarakt hastalarında değil, göz yapısı uygun olan farklı hasta gruplarında da değerlendirilebilir.
Lens seçiminde kornea ve retina sağlığı, gözün doğal lensinin durumu, kişinin yaşı ve günlük yaşam alışkanlıkları birlikte incelenir. Cerrahi uygulamanın uygunluğu ve beklenen yararları ayrıntılı muayene sonucunda belirlenir.
GÖRME İHTİYAÇLARINA UYGUN PLANLAMA Bir kişinin iş günü bilgisayar karşısında geçerken başka biri el işiyle uğraşabilir veya gününün büyük bölümünü açık havada geçirebilir. Aynı yaşta ve aynı gözlük numarasına sahip kişilerin bile görme öncelikleri farklı olabilir.
Bu nedenle lens seçiminde yalnızca göz ölçümlerini değil, kişinin günlük yaşamını da önemsiyorum.

Dünyanın farklı ülkelerinde yöresel sanat ve mimari izleri taşıyan yapıları araştıran Japon belgesel ekibi, Cide'nin Çakırlı köyüne geldi.
Japon zanaatkarların dünyayı dolaşarak gerçekleştirdikleri onarım ve yenileme çalışmalarının anlatıldığı belgesel programı kapsamında, 4 marangoz ve 2 taş ustası tarafından, 3 gün süren çalışmanın ardından 1966 yılında inşa edilen ilkokula yerden ısıtma sistemi kazandırıldı.
Proje direktörü Jo Ogaki, AA muhabirine, yaptıkları görüşmelerde bu okula bir şeyler yapmanın çok uygun olacağına karar verdiklerini söyledi.
Ustalarla Türkiye'ye geldiklerini anlatan Ogaki, "Japonya'daki üstün tekniğe sahip ustalar buraya geldi ve yaratıcı fikirlerle burayı yeni sistemle donattı. Yapılan şey hem bize hem de köye değer katmış oldu." dedi.
Dünyanın farklı bölgelerinde farklı projeler yaptıklarını ifade eden Ogaki, "Bu Türkiye'deki ikinci projemiz. İlkinde Düzce'de bir köyde eski bir su değirmenini onardık. Cide'deki çalışmanın ardından Türkiye'den ayrılacağız." diye konuştu.
Zaman zaman öğrencilerin kendilerini ziyarete geldiğini belirten Ogaki, "Öğrenciler ve köy sakinleri ile güzel iletişim kurduk. Öğrenciler geldiler, burayı ilgi çekici buldu. İnsanların yüzü güldü. Aslında bizim projemizin temel amacı insanları mutlu etmek. İnsanlar gülsün kendilerini iyi hissetsin. Bunu istiyoruz." ifadelerini kullandı.
Marangoz Tashiyuki Kawahara ise kışın soğuk olacağını düşündükleri sınıfı ısıtmak için yerden ısıtma sistemi kurduklarını söyledi.
Güzel bir ürün ortaya çıktığını aktaran Kawahara, "Bunu doğaya uyumlu bir şekilde yapmak istedik. Onun için yeri zeminde ısıtma sistemi yaptık. Marangoz ustaları zemini yaptı. Koridorda yanan sobada ısınan su sirkülasyon sistemi ile sınıfın tabanında dolaşıyor. Sıva ustamız da duvarı özel bir şekilde nemi alacak şekilde yaptı. Bu şekilde çocukların sağlığı için sınıfın havası kuru olmayacak. Bir marangozumuz da çocukların kullanabileceği raflar yaptı ama normal raf değil. Ufak boyda çocukların da erişebileceği şekilde ve daha sonra büyüdükten sonra sıra veya sandalye olarak da kullanabilecek şekilde yaptı." dedi.
Böyle bir şeye vesile olmaktan mutluluk duyduklarını dile getiren Kawahara, "Ustalar Vagonu diye bir programımız var. Japonya'dan farklı alandaki ustalar yurt dışında özellikle şehir merkezinden uzakta kalan böyle yerlere geliyoruz ve oradaki yerel halk için bir yardım dokunuşunda bulunmak istiyoruz. Böyle bir köyde bu projede yer almak bizim için onur verici oldu." diye konuştu.
Mert Yiğit Gün de 3. sınıf öğrencisi olduğunu ifade ederek, "Okulda 7 öğrenci bulunuyor. Birinci sınıf öğrencilerinin ayakları yetişmiyordu. Yere odun döşemesi yaptılar. Sıcak bir döşeme yaptılar.Teşekkür ederim." ifadelerini kullandı.
Zeynep Gün ise ilkokulu bu okulda okuduğunu kaydederek, "Şu an altıncı sınıfa geçtim. Okulumuz için Japonya'dan arkadaşlar geldi. Yerleri ısıtıcılı yaptılar. Kardeşim Mert de onlara bir mektup hazırlayarak, 'Japonya'dan gelip okulumuza ısıtıcı döşediğiniz için teşekkür ederiz. Sizi çok seviyoruz.' yazdı." dedi.

A Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace, the Nordic country's Ministry of Defense said Saturday.
The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.
According to Finland's Defense Ministry, the incursion happened at 12:34 p.m. local time (10:34 UTC/GMT) off the town of Loviisa, on the southern coast.
"This alleged airspace violation may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations carried out by Finland following damage sustained by a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland," public broadcaster YLE cited Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen as saying.
The ministry added the helicopter could have penetrated up to 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.
Earlier Saturday, Finland — one of NATO's newest members — said a Russian cargo ship heading for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad caught fire after being struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.
The Finnish military said the Sparta II was damaged ⁠west ⁠of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters.
Finnish ‌Border ​Guard Commander Ilja Iljin later told YLE that the vessel, which is known to have links to the Russian military, was struck by Ukrainian drones while in Russian waters.
"At the moment, ​there is no confirmed information ⁠about ​what cargo ​is on board, ​but it ‌cannot be ruled out ​that ⁠there is military materiel on ⁠board," ​Iljin said.
The ship is on a US sanctions list, according to a search of the Open Sanctions website.
The Border Guard later said the crew of the Sparta II was evacuating into a life raft and rescue boat.
"The [Ukraine] war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas," wrote Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on X.
Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," he added.
The Finnish government has put temporary curbs on aviation and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

Report and free match highlights as teenager Luca Williams-Barnett stars in Tottenham's 2-0 home win over Ipswich; the 18-year-old made Spurs history with his 15th-minute opener; England U19 international then involved in Dominic Solanke's second-half goal as Ipswich go five without a win
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett scored on his first Tottenham start to make history in Spurs’ 2-0 home win over Ipswich.
The 18-year-old bundled home the opener at the back post in the 15th minute to become the youngest Spurs player to score on his first Premier League start for the club.
The Spurs academy graduate then turned provider in the second half as he terrorised the Ipswich defence from his left-wing position to tee up Dominic Solanke with a low cross for a simple 51st-minute finish.
But Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton's diversion into Solanke's path meant Williams-Barnett was not officially credited with the assist.
It meant Williams-Barnett, at the age of 18 years and 51 days, just missed out on becoming the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game (Michael Owen in December 1997 at 17y 364d).
The teenager was substituted in the 64th minute to a standing ovation and rapturous cheers from the Spurs fans, who had serenaded Williams-Barnett with Harry Kane's 'He's one of our own' chant - raising hopes that the club may have unearthed a new academy hero.
The England U19 international's dazzling display inspired Tottenham to a third consecutive home league victory for the first time in two years, lifting Roberto De Zerbi's side to ninth and within three points of the top five.
But the Italian had to watch the deserved win from the stands as he served a one-game touchline ban after receiving three yellow cards this season.
His opposite number Gary O'Neil, meanwhile, saw his side's winless run extend to five games as Ipswich rarely threatened the home side to leave the Tractor Boys in 16th and just two points above the relegation zone.
Spurs head coach De Zerbi believes Williams-Barnett is a "special player" and is a similar talent to Barcelona teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.
De Zerbi said at his post-match press conference: "He is a special player. I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think.
"He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.
"Yesterday evening, when I gave the first 11 to the players, I said, 'remember your debut and help the kid tomorrow, because he's one of us and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game'.
"He's very young but at the same time he's a mature guy. He understands the right behaviour to keep in the dressing room - and he's older than his age."
He added: "The first day I spoke with Luca, I asked him two things: to play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom and to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way, and the first defenders are really the attackers; even if they are Ballon d'Or winners or any players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."
Then asked whether Williams-Barnett is a special talent like PSG's Ballon d'Or winner Dembele and Spain's World Cup-winner Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so.
"One of the best things in my career as a player, I've seen today on the bus from the training ground to the stadium. He was very close to me on the bus, and while we were coming to the stadium, he was watching Ronaldinho and Hazard on YouTube.
"I thought he was a special guy because, one hour and 30 minutes before your debut in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, [Eden] Hazard, Neymar, all this type of talent.
"Football is magic, no? The qualities, okay, but also the passion - you understand football, how football can be."
Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil speaking at his post-match press conference:
"Many of us weren't quite able to get to the level that we're used to. A tough afternoon.
"I didn't enjoy it, but I did enjoy watching the lads dig in and find a way to keep going together in a tough moment because that's what we need.
"Between the goals and after the goals, we were okay, and we arrived in the final third enough to cause problems, but we didn't.
"Disappointing, but it was a big task coming here and we needed things to be perfect."
After a handful of encouraging substitute displays this season, the 18-year-old was deservedly handed his first Spurs start - and boy did he take it.
He dazzled on the left wing to become the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).
Bale would go on to become a Spurs great, and there will be optimism that Williams-Barnett can do the same.
Every time he touched the ball in the win over Ipswich, there was real excitement at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which has been in short supply in recent times.
He was a constant threat to the Ipswich defence as defenders backed off him, which exactly led to Solanke's goal.
The stats back up his impressive performance - he had the most touches in the opposition box (8) and big chances (2) of any player, while no player had more than his four shots on target.
For all of Spurs' big summer spending, their new hero looks to be from within.

Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.
That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.
Harry Winks was the last academy graduate to score on his debut more than a decade ago – a feat that Kane also achieved two years earlier against Sunderland. Yet after Spurs decided to allow the England Under-21s striker Will Lankshear to join Middlesbrough in the summer, there was no chance that Williams-Barnett would be allowed to follow him out of the door. He became the 900th player ever to represent Spurs when he made his debut last year and the teenager left the field here to a standing ovation that he will never forget.
“I told him to play like he plays in the park with his friends, with the same freedom,” said De Zerbi. “And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembélé, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal. Luca is a special player. I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He’s very young but at same time he’s very mature. He is older than his age.”
Asked whether his protege has the potential to be compared to the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi added: “Yes, I think so. One of the best things in my career I’ve seen today on the bus to the stadium. He was watching [clips] on YouTube of Ronaldinho, Hazard. I think he’s a special guy, because if one hour before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. Having the qualities is one thing but he has the passion for football, too.”
After a promising start to the campaign, Ipswich’s momentum has stalled – they have now gone five games without a victory. But Gary O’Neil, who has already seen 16-year-old Max Dowman score twice for Arsenal against his side in the Carabao Cup, acknowledged that they had been second best throughout. “You need things to be perfect when we come to a place like this and we didn’t make things easy for ourselves,” he said.
De Zerbi dropped a huge hint that Williams-Barnett could be handed his opportunity to start after two impressive cameos against Crystal Palace and Leeds. “Maybe, maybe,” he said on Friday. It turned out that the decision was actually taken last week, although the absence of Sandro Tonali due to illness forced Spurs into a reshuffle in midfield as Mateus Fernandes was handed the holding role.
Solanke has struggled to fill the void left by Kane since joining from Bournemouth in 2024 but looked in determined mood and he was inches wide with a swivel and shot from inside the area. A driving run from Williams-Barnett had the home supporters off their feet, with Solanke again going close from the resulting corner. It then needed a timely block from the teenager to stop Ipswich breaking downfield.
His big moment arrived less than 60 seconds later. Porro’s ball to the back post should have been dealt with by Abdoul Ouattara, only for a moment’s hesitation to allow Williams-Barnett to muscle in front of him and apply the finish with his knee. “He’s one of our own,” sang the Tottenham fans in delight.
Mohammed Kudus was unfortunate to see his superb effort from a free-kick cannon off the inside of the post and away to safety. Williams-Barnett will be disappointed not to have scored his second when he miskicked inside the six-yard box with the goal gaping. James Maddison was then denied by a brilliant save from Christian Walton and Williams-Barnett left the field at half-time looking very pleased with himself as he waved to his family in the crowd.
His smile grew even broader after Darnell Furlong was left bamboozled by a direct run down the left flank before the youngster delivered the ball on a plate for Solanke to score his first goal here since March. The defeat could have been worse for Ipswich had it not been for Walton, and O’Neil will know they are in danger of being sucked into trouble if this winless run continues. There are no such concerns for Tottenham these days. Thanks to Williams-Barnett, their future looks much brighter than a few weeks ago.

Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".
The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior goal and then played a pivotal role in Dominic Solanke's second as Spurs comfortably beat Ipswich 2-0 at home .
Yet what might be a sign of the excitement about his potential was manager Roberto de Zerbi calmly explaining that "his talent is bigger than this performance".
The Tottenham boss obviously believes this is just the beginning for the talented teenager.
Williams-Barnett became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007.
They would be pretty impressive footsteps to follow in if he was to get close to the player Bale once was for the north London club.
But for the slightest of touches on his fizzed ball across the area from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton before Solanke turned home, Williams-Barnett would have become the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, aged just 18 years and 51 days old.
Only Michael Owen, who did it at 17 years and 364 days for Liverpool in 1997, would have done it at a younger age.
"He's incredible, honestly," Solanke told Final Score. "We get to see him every day in training so we know what a player he is - the confidence he has, the ability he has.
"The world got to see it today, which is great for him. His confidence and ability is amazing. He'll help us a lot."
'Unbelievable' - How Spurs youngster Williams-Barnett impressed on first start
Williams-Barnett was born in Luton and played for his hometown club before moving to Spurs at the age of 10.
The teenager has been generating excitement with his performances for the club's underage teams for some time.
Back in the 2023-24 season, he played for Tottenham 's Under-18s aged just 15 and in the following campaign he scored the Under-18 Premier League goal of the season against Leicester having become renowned for fine long-range strikes.
Williams-Barnett has been around Tottenham 's first-team since the 2024-25 campaign as he was on the bench for three Europa League games and a Premier League match but his debut came last season as a substitute in a Carabao Cup game against Doncaster Rovers under previous boss Thomas Frank.
Last December, he scored five goals in a Under-19 UEFA Youth League game against Slavia Prague.
Williams-Barnett featured in the EFL Cup as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton in August before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.
Yet it was still a bold choice from De Zerbi to make Williams-Barnett the club's sixth youngest starter in Premier League history given Spurs were coming into this game on the back of a defeat by Leeds United which checked a recent upturn in form.
However, the Spurs boss was rewarded with a man-of-the-match worthy display.
His goal was one of endeavour as he brushed in front of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.
Throughout the game, he was looking for the ball constantly and not afraid to run with it and try to make things happen.
"Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he shows his quality," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie told BBC Match of the Day.
"Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing."
The winger was unfortunate not to get the assist but the goal does not happen without his powerful cross.
The England youth international was not afraid to take on a shot and his four attempts were all on target while he had a passing accuracy of 77.4% among his 44 touches.
Only Solanke took on more shots in the game with four of his five on target.
"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy," added Solanke.
"He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like.
"But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that."
Roberto De Zerbi post-match interview - Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town
Williams-Barnett was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute which brought a standing ovation from the crowd but, with the Brazilian then being forced off later on with an injury, there may be more opportunities in the coming weeks.
Obviously there will be more excitement about the talented teenager now which De Zerbi will have to manage and he has picked midfielder James Maddison as a good mentor for the attacker.
"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," the Spurs boss told BBC Match of the Day.
"It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.
"The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham 's dressing room now is a good environment for him.
"I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.
"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea .
The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.
It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.
Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton , Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.
From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.
The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea .
"Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.
"We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games."
The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.
Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton .
After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose said: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.
"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."
Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak is a club record - beating two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13
Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth 's results.
However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.
Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.
It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?
It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.
The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.
In addition to wins over Sunderland , Manchester United , Leeds , Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.
Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.
Bournemouth are currently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.
"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.
Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth 's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham .
'I'll call him' - Justin Kluivert happy he's scored same week as dad Patrick
One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth 's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.
After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.
Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.
In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.
Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.
By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.
"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team."
It is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.
That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.
"The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive."
The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.
What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.
Bournemouth 's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.
Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.
So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?
Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?
Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.
"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.
"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.
"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.
"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form."

Marco Rose saluted the in-form Evanilson after the Brazilian scored for a sixth Premier League game in a row to lift Bournemouth up to fourth place with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest .
Evanilson’s brilliantly taken 19th-minute opener set his side on course for a club record ninth straight win in all competitions, while the defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win against Manchester City before the international break.
Rose said: “We defend together as a team, and we attack together as a team, but the forward guys were excellent today. They did a great job scoring the goals and the other guys support them. Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a No 9, really beautiful goals so I am happy.”
Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva.
Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels.
Bournemouth took the lead in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-foot shot into the roof of the net.
Justin Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from 20 yards which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area.
Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of teammate Tyler Adams. But Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier.
Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to find a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for Morgan Gibbs-White but the captain could not properly connect with his header.
• Bournemouth have won five successive games in the top-flight of English football for the first time. Only Arsenal (67, before Newcastle game) and Manchester City (60) have collected more Premier League points in 2026 than the Cherries (52 – W13 D13 L4).
• Bournemouth have won each of their last nine games in all competitions, their longest ever such run, overtaking two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13.
• Nottingham Forest failed to score in this game despite registering 2.14 expected goals, the highest xG tally by any team not to score in a Premier League match this season. Opta
James McAtee ballooned an effort over the bar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. The substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested the underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper, Djordje Petrovic.
Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and Bournemouth’s third when he stung the gloves of Sels from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.
Glasner, whose side had 19 shots but only one on target, said: “Of course when you lose it’s always a tough 90 minutes, especially when you make too many mistakes like we did in the first half.
“The second goal straight before half-time was a little bit of a killer but credit to the lads in the second half for finding a filter back into the game. We had some good situations, but we couldn’t convert them.
“We are not able to score in this game, and this is what we have to look at and where we have to improve. We took too many touches, and were not so aggressive.”
